drivers.lead: Vergne completed the only back-to-back pair in the championship's history in 2019, and Wehrlein drew level with a second title in 2026
drivers.note: Twelve seasons, ten different champions, and nobody has won three — the record is two, and it has been shared only since Pascal Wehrlein's second, taken at the London finale in August 2026. Jean-Éric Vergne set it first, winning in 2018 and 2019 for Techeetah, and he remains the only driver to have defended a Formula E title: the first four seasons produced four different winners, and no one has repeated in consecutive years since either. Wehrlein's two are two years apart, 2024 and 2026 with Porsche, with Oliver Rowland's Nissan title in between. Eight of the ten champions have won exactly once. That spread is what stands in the way of a third — no Formula E driver has ever won two in a row and then added another, and only Vergne has managed even the first half of it.

teams.lead: Renault e.dams won the first three teams' titles, 2015 to 2017, and the partnership was gone a season later
teams.note: The team was entered as e.dams-Renault in the opening season and as Renault e.dams after that, and it took the teams' championship in all three. At the end of the 2018 season Renault turned its attention back to Formula 1 and handed its half of the partnership to Nissan, so this record has belonged to a team that stopped existing under that name before the championship's fifth season. Nobody has matched three since. DS Techeetah won in 2019 and 2020, Mercedes-EQ in 2021 and 2022 — immediately before Mercedes left the championship outright to concentrate on Formula 1 — and Jaguar TCS Racing in 2024 and 2026. Jaguar is the only one of the three to have won anything in the last three seasons, which makes it the one team with a live route to the record.
